name: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione (19-norandrostenedione)
lead: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione, also called 19-norandrostenedione or bolandione, is a steroid that is a precursor of nandrolone. It was sold over the counter in the US as a prohormone supplement until 2005.[2]

It is best documented in the literature through doping research. A 2000 JAMA study found trace contamination of over-the-counter androstenedione products and examined whether androstenedione and 19-norandrostenedione ingestion causes positive urine tests for a nandrolone metabolite.[1]

paras: Wikipedia reports that it converts readily to nandrolone orally and binds the androgen receptor about ten times less potently than DHT.[2] It is also a 19-nor steroid like those found naturally in small quantities, for example in human ovarian follicular fluid, where 19-norandrostenedione and 19-nortestosterone have been measured.[3]

Because it and nandrolone share the urinary metabolite 19-norandrosterone, contaminated supplements can yield positive tests.[1][2] A registered phase 1/2 trial (started 2006, 20 participants) studied the risk of positive doping tests after ingesting supplements contaminated with trace nandrolone metabolites.[4]

The 2000 JAMA study assessed the purity of over-the-counter androstenedione and whether administration of androstenedione or 19-norandrostenedione leads to positive tests for a nandrolone metabolite.[1] A completed trial, NCT00682123, evaluated positive-test risk from contaminated supplements.[4] No trials have evaluated muscle or appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: JAMA study on trace contamination and nandrolone-metabolite positives.[1]

card.summary: A nandrolone prohormone from the supplement era, now mostly a doping-control footnote.
card.note: Controlled in the US; prohibited in sport; can cause positive nandrolone tests.

quick.overview:
19-Norandrostenedione is a prohormone that converts to nandrolone. It was sold as a supplement in the US until 2005.

Research on it centres on doping tests rather than muscle outcomes.
quick.mechanism: After oral intake it converts to nandrolone and shares its urinary metabolite.
quick.risks: US Schedule III, banned in sport. Contaminated supplements have caused positive nandrolone tests.
